chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarququfi, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who intends to go to Makkah or Al-Madina, who dislikes that he goes out with a weapon in his possession. He said: 'There is no harm in him going out with the weapon from his city, but when he enters Makkah, he should not display it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on carrying and displaying weapons in Makkah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between the right to carry arms for protection during travel and the requirement of *hurma* (sanctity) within the sacred precincts of Makkah. It reflects the scholarly understanding that while weapons are permitted for security, their open display (*izhar*) is discouraged to maintain the spiritual tranquility and reverence appropriate for the House of Allah.
